hero.caption: As seen in September 2021, a historic plaque marks the crest of the low hill at the northeast corner of Seneca Street and Ridge Road in West Seneca, New York as the former site of the Onondaga village of Chief Big Sky, which "consisted of twenty-eight cabins in good repair in 1791". Though Erie County was not initially Onondaga territory, the region served as a refuge for many survivors of the bloody Sullivan-Clinton Expedition of 1779, an American Revolutionary War campaign during which its namesakes, Major General John Sullivan and Brigadier General James Clinton of the Continental Army, marauded through the Iroquois territory of Central New York in retribution for attacks carried out by them and their British and Loyalist allies against Patriot separatists in Cobleskill, Wyoming Valley and Cherry Valley. The fate of Big Sky's village is unrecorded, but at the time almost the entirety of West Seneca was contained within the Buffalo Creek Reservation of the Seneca Nation (allies of the Onondaga), which was dissolved in 1842.

images.filename: Sisters of Charity Hospital, Buffalo, New York - 20200923.jpg
images.caption: Sisters of Charity Hospital, 2157 Main Street, Buffalo, New York, September 2020. The oldest hospital in Buffalo, Sisters traces its history to 1848 - the year after the founding of the city's Roman Catholic diocese - as a way of addressing both the general lack of organized health care in the city as well as the anti-Catholic sentiment that pervaded the city's institutional structure. An initial spate of controversy over the state legislature's use of public funds to prop up a religious facility was rendered moot by the hospital's exemplary performance during the city's 1849-50 cholera epidemic. The hospital's original location in what's now the Allentown neighborhood was superseded in 1876 by a larger facility at the corner of Main Street and Delavan Avenue (currently the site of Canisius College's Koessler Athletic Center), which itself was replaced in 1946 by the current facility.
images.alt: Sisters of Charity Hospital, 2157 Main Street, Buffalo, New York, September 2020.
